note: Several lint rules and the shared parser were O(n^2) in physical line length (node --cpu-prof: unanchored \w+-shaped regexes backtracking on one long uninterrupted \w-run -- move-parser.mjs's multiplication, division and parameter-name regexes, MOV-003's own copy of the division shape, MOV-005's \w+::contains / \w+::has patterns and its discarded-call name lookup, and MOV-001's Cap/Key test). MOV-005 is exercised with a long identifier because a 40,000-digit literal is expected to be rejected by the Move compiler (not re-verified against a toolchain). The fix anchors each unanchored \w+ operand to the start of its word-run (a (?<!\w) lookbehind), drops the quantifier where the pattern only needed one word character, and tests MOV-001's Cap/Key per word, so every run is tried once and each regex captures the same whole name at any length. No \w{1,128} bound is used on a compared name: past 128 characters a bounded capture slides or refuses (changing a verdict in either direction), and truncating both sides of a comparison makes names that differ only after the bound collide. The one remaining bound is the parser's function-call regex, whose captured name is displayed and never compared. Also hoisted MOV-002's redundant source.split('\n') (recomputed on every multiplication match, and again before the shift-detection pass) to run once. Findings must be identical to the pre-fix rules on every real fixture; only wall-clock behaviour changes. Every operand position that reads a long name is pinned in both directions (safe reads 0, unsafe reads 1) at 120/128/129/140/200 characters. Loose timing tripwires (40k-digit and 40k-char fixtures under generous ceilings, explicitly not a strict perf SLA) and a sweep of every rule file against thirteen long-identifier shapes catch a return to O(n^2), including in a rule added later.
